# The Concierge (front-desk shim — the address verb)

This file is a **thin shim** — the harness-discoverable trigger for the Concierge. The organ is
the canon entry `Palace development/Concierge.md` ([[Concierge]]); the machinery is
`_ops/concierge/` (the **charter** `prompts/companion.md`, the **posture** prompts, `README.md`
for the full dispatch spec). Per [[Skills Are Enchantable Pages]], the page is the organ and this
file is one dispatch surface onto it — read the canon entry and machinery rather than duplicating
them.

You are the working Claude, addressing the palace's **resident companion** — one agent you spawn
once and keep for the session. Your job: **spawn-or-resume it, name the posture, relay the
product.** The search never enters this conversation; only the finished thing does.

## The lifecycle — resident, not fresh-per-request

0. **Summon at the open.** When to summon, and that it be seen, is the rule in [[CHILD]] § Growing
   up. Where the surface cannot spawn, say so at the open instead. Step 1 *is* that spawn; the
   rest is how.

1. **The spawn — one resident, and keep the agent ID.** Spawn one write-capable
   resident — subagent_type **`palace-writer`** ([[Agent Toolbox]] profile: sheds ~20K of unused
   MCP schemas vs `general-purpose`, ~30K vs 46K, and still writes so the curator posture works from
   the same resident) — with the **charter** (`prompts/companion.md`); the charter has it grow at boot —
   ELDER, SCHEMA, then the **operational tier** as its standing expertise (SUBSTRATE · ROSETTA · Substrate Skill ·
   Palace Ceremonies · STIGMERGY + wire spec) — deeper in *how the palace runs* than you, so it
   validates/supports the palace in parallel while you work the task. Record its `agentId`.
   **Spawn it without a `name`.** With agent teams enabled (`CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS`,
   on in Loudon's terminal sessions), a *named* Agent call launches a teammate, not a subagent: its
   returns come back as idle notifications, cut off at a fixed length and arriving late and twice,
   and the resume carries no `<usage>` block, so the dial below goes blind. Unnamed, it stays a
   subagent in every mode — its result arrives whole, once, with its token count — and it is still
   resumable by `SendMessage` to the held ID. (Docs: code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents § Subagent
   names; verified across 23 session transcripts 2026-09-26 — the failures were exactly the named
   spawns in CLI sessions.)
2. **Every later address → resume the same agent** (`SendMessage` to the held ID), naming the
   posture and filling that posture prompt's slots. It carries its prior context forward — don't
   re-spawn, and don't re-feed what it already holds. After a compaction the ID may be missing from the summary: find it in the session's `subagents/` folder and resume that one before spawning another ([[Concierge]] § The mechanism).
3. **Watch its health with the dial.** Each resume returns `subagent_tokens` in the Agent tool's
   `<usage>` block — the objective read (never its self-report). Pass it to the dial:
   `node _ops/concierge/dial.mjs --tokens <N> --model <companion-model>`. Headline is **trust** = capacity
   (÷ window): fine below ~60%, watch 60–80%, degraded past 80% — only capacity says respawn-for-reliability.
   A separate **cost** note (from absolute load) flags when resumes get expensive — respawn-to-save, not a
   trust alarm. Parked between addresses it costs nothing. Same dial serves the close (`--for close`), where
   how spent the parent is leads.

If you expect a genuinely large fan-out, tell Loudon the rough cost first (his standing preference).

## Triage — classify the address, name the posture

| The address sounds like… | Posture | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| "find / collect / gather every doc/link/entry about X" — wants the **material** | **gatherer** (read-only) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/gatherer.md` |
| "what does the palace say about X / how does Z work" — wants an **answer** | **oracle Q&A** (read-only, may web-verify) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/oracle-qa.md` |
| "what should I work on / what's open / I'm back" — wants **one move**, not a pile | **scout** (read-only) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/scout.md` |
| "tidy / tend the links around what I touched" | **curator** (writes) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/curator.md` |
| "close this session well" | **moderator** (at the close) | not this skill — the `close well` trigger, which **resumes this same resident** by the ID you held (`_ops/closing-well/dispatch.md` § Path A) |
| anything a cheap file-read settles | — | just read the file; don't address |

Fill the posture prompt's slots — `{{REQUEST}}` / `{{QUESTION}}` / `{{TOUCHED_ENTRIES}}`,
`{{TRANSCRIPT_CONTEXT}}`, `{{PALACE_ROOT}}` = the palace folder this session was started in: its
worktree or clone, and `/Users/loudonstearns/Documents/The Palace` only when the session runs there.
For a conversation-dependent address, distill the transcript
(`node _ops/closing-well/transcript-reader.mjs --resolve --session <id>` → `--distill --session <id>`); for a self-contained
one, a 2–3 line note is enough.

## Relay — and hold the safety line

Relay the product as returned (already file-cited). For the **curator**: report what it *did*
(reversible), **surface its `offer`s for Loudon's yes; on his yes, address the Concierge again to apply them — the child session does not write the house**, and pass
along its flags and anything it web-verified. The companion's heavy bias is to draft, not act;
your job on the other end is to keep the review real — drafts get read, not rubber-stamped.
Hand each offer on as the curator wrote it — its plain sentence, every rule it writes down, its exact words — and if you have promised Loudon the words, show them; a summary in their place is said aloud as a summary.

## The guard (carry it every time)

palace's silence is a real answer, never a confabulated one. Keep this shim thin — when the model
changes, change `_ops/concierge/README.md`, `prompts/companion.md`, and the canon entry, not this

54

56	
57	Loud'n Live is Loudon's professional persona, online and in person: the container for what he chooses to present to the world. It is honest, but it is his teaching and coaching face, not the whole of him. It starts soon as YouTube videos and livestreams for electronic musicians.

59	**A moving target.** It grows and adapts as Loudon does. This page has been a curriculum platform, a channel and a whole public self, and older versions still turn up around the palace. When another page disagrees with this one, this one is current. There is no hard line between Loud'n Live and his other projects: some work ends up here, some elsewhere.
60	
61	## The parts, right now
62	
63	- **[[LDN RTM]]** — *Read The Manual*: one product's whole manual, read, tested, and covered one short video per section. The format, the rig, and the queue of manuals live there. The same rig records Loudon's audio commentary on student projects — for the students, not for a public catalog.
64	- **One-on-one coaching** — the established part, in person and online.
65	- **Destination retreats** — on the horizon: beautiful places, focused work, a creative learning environment, and a cohort that connects. In the vein of wellness retreats.
66	- **YouTube videos and livestreams for electronic musicians** — starting soon. One project pushed forward at a time: some deep dives into the foundations of sound, some hands-on builds, some music technique, some detours into theory or debugging. No outcome promises; the working is the deliverable. Any project in the palace can turn up here.
67	
68	New parts join when they exist. Loose descriptors are welcome; the name holds the whole, not a format.
69	
70	## Beside it, for now
71	
72	- **[[BLUELINE]] and Loudon's music** — his own creative work, public but not yet inside Loud'n Live.
73	- **Most of the palace.** Loudon expects much of the palace, and the palace as a system, to come inside in time.
74	
75	Underneath all of it is the palace's public face: the provenance layer, the record of where each project came from. Anyone can walk into the palace by two doors. The first is the **read view**, live at https://loudon-stearns.github.io/the-palace/: [[STIGMERGY]]'s STATE deck built static and read-only — PULSE, TOPOLOGY, TREE and the entry reader — and rebuilt on every push to `main`. It shows an entry's faces (the text, the rich face where there is one, the scroll's making) and leaves its memory in git: the Context, the ledger, the baton, and the board. The second is **git** itself: the public repository carries the whole house. Widening the public surface past these two waits for Loudon's own yes and a clean [[Sentry]] gate (`node _ops/sentry/sweep.mjs --gate`).
76	
77	## What the palace's public face holds back
78	
79	Narrow, on purpose. Loudon wants anyone curious to come away with a full, honest picture of him — "those interested can understand who I am through exploring" — so the read view shows who he is and what he plans, [[Palace To-Do]] and the audits included, and keeps back only highly personal data and anything that puts his finances at risk. For now it stays out of search engines (a robots noindex on every page), and Loudon will revisit that.
80	
81	## Editorial posture
82	
83	**Subject is sound and music; tools are the medium.** Loudon Live is not a tools brand. Specific software, hardware, and code appear when the work requires them. The lasting questions — how a sound is shaped, why a phrase works, what your ears are doing — outlive any particular tool.
84	
85	**Honesty is a light touch, not a confession.** The work-in-progress nature of the whole is named once and then left alone; the work speaks. Rigor about craft, no pretense about progress.
86	
87	**Loud'n Live is itself a teaching artifact.** It models a way of working — choosing a project, naming a loose goal, working through the wall, talking through the thinking — that teaches better than any one piece of content can.
88	
89	## The look
90	
91	The [[Loudon Live Design System]] is the look — palettes, type, stream cards, overlays — and it is now the palace's default dress (`_ops/loudon-live/design-system/`). Channel copy and stream-card templates live in this entry's bundle as the launch kit.
92	
93	The visual signature is the Lissajous trace inside a sphere — see [[Hyperdimensional Prism]] for the identity essay. It reads at several depths at once: an oscilloscope trace to a producer, a path through knowledge space to a learner, a method made visible to a collaborator. The patch that *generates* the logo is itself a teaching object anyone can download, modify, and run.
94

96	
97	Electronic musicians, to start; in time, creative coaching for people who learn across fields on their own ([[Autodidact Polymaths]]).
98

100	
101	- **Always-positive, always-supportive-of-makers.** From the RTM stance in [[Loudon's Toolkit]] — toward the tools and the people who build them.
102	- **The instrument teaches while it sounds.** Specific to general: the [[2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer]] is *a concrete entry point to 2D Fourier analysis, torus geometry, quasi-periodicity, bifurcation theory, and quasicrystal mathematics.*
103	- **Teaching as a Confucian act.** [[Confucianism]] names the teacher-student relationship here as a worked reading of *ren* and *li* — the relational ethic of the whole.
104	- **Theatrical, dub-lineage interface mythology where it fits.** Some instruments carry deliberate mythological framing (the séance-medium-as-dub-engineer in [[Retrospective Delay]]); teaching doesn't require sober affect.

108	- **A scaffolded curriculum.** Every project cut into five sessions, mapped by prerequisite, the Four Pillars as its spine, a launch in September 2026. Drawn in April 2026, set down 2026-09-26 in favor of a looser presence building slowly. Its map is archived as [[Loudon Live — Curriculum Map]].
109	- **Loudon Live as a reputation engine** for later income (manufacturer-sponsored teaching, an original hardware line). Set down; those hopes stay Loudon's own in [[Loudon's Toolkit]].
110	- **Loudon Live as his whole public self** (2026-09-26 to 2026-10-14): narrowed to his teaching and coaching face.

116	- **Live moments.** Recorded long-form, live streams, build-alongs, Q&As, jam sessions — which, and when? Undecided, and the first real ones should teach it.
117	- **What funds it, if anything.** Ad revenue, membership, paid courses — not decided, and not urgent.
118	- **Streams and the projects they touch.** Does a stream want a typed link from this page, or does it live on the project's scroll as a made thing?

# Loudon Live

![[Loudon Live — hero.png]]

Loud'n Live is Loudon's professional persona, online and in person: the container for what he chooses to present to the world. It is honest, but it is his teaching and coaching face, not the whole of him. It starts soon as YouTube videos and livestreams for electronic musicians.

**A moving target.** It grows and adapts as Loudon does. This page has been a curriculum platform, a channel and a whole public self, and older versions still turn up around the palace. When another page disagrees with this one, this one is current. There is no hard line between Loud'n Live and his other projects: some work ends up here, some elsewhere.

## The parts, right now

- **[[LDN RTM]]** — *Read The Manual*: one product's whole manual, read, tested, and covered one short video per section. The format, the rig, and the queue of manuals live there. The same rig records Loudon's audio commentary on student projects — for the students, not for a public catalog.
- **One-on-one coaching** — the established part, in person and online.
- **Destination retreats** — on the horizon: beautiful places, focused work, a creative learning environment, and a cohort that connects. In the vein of wellness retreats.
- **YouTube videos and livestreams for electronic musicians** — starting soon. One project pushed forward at a time: some deep dives into the foundations of sound, some hands-on builds, some music technique, some detours into theory or debugging. No outcome promises; the working is the deliverable. Any project in the palace can turn up here.

New parts join when they exist. Loose descriptors are welcome; the name holds the whole, not a format.

## Beside it, for now

- **[[BLUELINE]] and Loudon's music** — his own creative work, public but not yet inside Loud'n Live.
- **Most of the palace.** Loudon expects much of the palace, and the palace as a system, to come inside in time.

Underneath all of it is the palace's public face: the provenance layer, the record of where each project came from. Anyone can walk into the palace by two doors. The first is the **read view**, live at https://loudon-stearns.github.io/the-palace/: [[STIGMERGY]]'s STATE deck built static and read-only — PULSE, TOPOLOGY, TREE and the entry reader — and rebuilt on every push to `main`. It shows an entry's faces (the text, the rich face where there is one, the scroll's making) and leaves its memory in git: the Context, the ledger, the baton, and the board. The second is **git** itself: the public repository carries the whole house. Widening the public surface past these two waits for Loudon's own yes and a clean [[Sentry]] gate (`node _ops/sentry/sweep.mjs --gate`).

## What the palace's public face holds back

Narrow, on purpose. Loudon wants anyone curious to come away with a full, honest picture of him — "those interested can understand who I am through exploring" — so the read view shows who he is and what he plans, [[Palace To-Do]] and the audits included, and keeps back only highly personal data and anything that puts his finances at risk. For now it stays out of search engines (a robots noindex on every page), and Loudon will revisit that.

## Editorial posture

**Subject is sound and music; tools are the medium.** Loudon Live is not a tools brand. Specific software, hardware, and code appear when the work requires them. The lasting questions — how a sound is shaped, why a phrase works, what your ears are doing — outlive any particular tool.

**Honesty is a light touch, not a confession.** The work-in-progress nature of the whole is named once and then left alone; the work speaks. Rigor about craft, no pretense about progress.

**Loud'n Live is itself a teaching artifact.** It models a way of working — choosing a project, naming a loose goal, working through the wall, talking through the thinking — that teaches better than any one piece of content can.

## The look

The [[Loudon Live Design System]] is the look — palettes, type, stream cards, overlays — and it is now the palace's default dress (`_ops/loudon-live/design-system/`). Channel copy and stream-card templates live in this entry's bundle as the launch kit.

The visual signature is the Lissajous trace inside a sphere — see [[Hyperdimensional Prism]] for the identity essay. It reads at several depths at once: an oscilloscope trace to a producer, a path through knowledge space to a learner, a method made visible to a collaborator. The patch that *generates* the logo is itself a teaching object anyone can download, modify, and run.

## The audience

Electronic musicians, to start; in time, creative coaching for people who learn across fields on their own ([[Autodidact Polymaths]]).

## How it teaches

- **Always-positive, always-supportive-of-makers.** From the RTM stance in [[Loudon's Toolkit]] — toward the tools and the people who build them.
- **The instrument teaches while it sounds.** Specific to general: the [[2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer]] is *a concrete entry point to 2D Fourier analysis, torus geometry, quasi-periodicity, bifurcation theory, and quasicrystal mathematics.*
- **Teaching as a Confucian act.** [[Confucianism]] names the teacher-student relationship here as a worked reading of *ren* and *li* — the relational ethic of the whole.
- **Theatrical, dub-lineage interface mythology where it fits.** Some instruments carry deliberate mythological framing (the séance-medium-as-dub-engineer in [[Retrospective Delay]]); teaching doesn't require sober affect.

## Lost branches

- **A scaffolded curriculum.** Every project cut into five sessions, mapped by prerequisite, the Four Pillars as its spine, a launch in September 2026. Drawn in April 2026, set down 2026-09-26 in favor of a looser presence building slowly. Its map is archived as [[Loudon Live — Curriculum Map]].
- **Loudon Live as a reputation engine** for later income (manufacturer-sponsored teaching, an original hardware line). Set down; those hopes stay Loudon's own in [[Loudon's Toolkit]].
- **Loudon Live as his whole public self** (2026-09-26 to 2026-10-14): narrowed to his teaching and coaching face.
- **Front-and-center confessional framing:** rejected as the primary register.
- **Tools-first identity:** rejected.

## Open Questions

- **Live moments.** Recorded long-form, live streams, build-alongs, Q&As, jam sessions — which, and when? Undecided, and the first real ones should teach it.
- **What funds it, if anything.** Ad revenue, membership, paid courses — not decided, and not urgent.
- **Streams and the projects they touch.** Does a stream want a typed link from this page, or does it live on the project's scroll as a made thing?
- **Search engines.** When does the read view drop its noindex?

> Live creative-tech build. Today's project: [one line, no promises].
>
> Tools today: [keep it loose — whatever fits the project].
>
> No outcome promises — this is a working stream. Hang out, ask questions in chat.
>
> ---
> About the channel: [paste your short About line]
> More on what I'm building: [optional, link if you have one]
>
> Chapters will be added after the stream ends.

## 5. OBS scene copy

Copy you'd burn into images or render as text overlays. Short, calm, low-stakes.

**Starting Soon (full-screen card)**

- Headline: `Starting soon`
- Subhead (pick one):
  - `Loudon Live · creative-tech workshop`
  - `Setting up · stream begins shortly`
  - `Pre-flight · grab a drink`
- Footer line (optional): `Today: [one-line topic]`

**BRB / short break**

- Headline: `Back in a minute`
- Subhead options:
  - `Quick break · stream resumes shortly`
  - `Coffee, then back to it`
  - `Working through a thing offscreen`

**Stream ended / Thanks**

- Headline: `That's the stream`
- Subhead options:
  - `Thanks for hanging out`
  - `VOD will stay up · subscribe for the next one`
  - `See you next time`
- Optional small footer: `Loudon Live · loudonlive on YouTube`

**Lower-third / on-screen labels** (pre-build these as transparent PNGs you can toggle)

- `Now building: [project]`
- `Tool in focus: [name the tool]`
- `Topic: [sound · technique · build · theory]`
- `Detour: [theory / debug / sidequest]`
- `Chat is open · questions welcome`
- `Loudon Live` (small, persistent watermark — corner)

**Opening monologue script (first ~30–45 sec of every stream)**

Use this as scaffolding, not a script to read.

> Hey, welcome in. I'm Loudon, this is Loudon Live.
>
> Today's project: [one sentence — what you're working on, what tool, what the loose goal is].
>
> Format as always: I'll work, I'll talk through what I'm doing, and chat is open the whole time. If you want me to slow down, explain something, or take a different angle, say so.
>
> Quick housekeeping: [optional — anything stream-specific]. Otherwise, let's get into it.

## 6. Going-live announcement posts

Short, neutral, copy-paste ready. Avoid hashtag spam.

**X / Bluesky (≤280 chars, post when stream goes live)**

Variant A:
> Going live now on Loudon Live. Today: [one-line topic].
> [YouTube live URL]

Variant B (when you don't want to name the topic):
> Stream's up. Loudon Live, working on something synth-shaped.
> [YouTube live URL]

Variant C (low-key recurring):
> Live now — creative tech, building out loud.
> [YouTube live URL]

**Pre-stream "tonight" post (a few hours before, optional)**

> Streaming tonight at [time] [tz]. Loudon Live, on YouTube.
> Working on: [one line, vague is fine].
> [channel URL]

**Instagram (caption — image post or story)**

> Live tonight on YouTube · Loudon Live
> [Time] [Timezone]
> Working on [one-line topic — keep it loose].
> Link in bio.
>
> #creativetech #musictech #synthesis #dsp #ableton #rnbo #maxmsp

If posting from a Story, just: `LIVE NOW` + sticker link to the YouTube URL. Don't overthink it.

**Generic ultra-short (Discord / group chat / wherever)**

> Live now: [URL]

## 7. Media & asset list — MVP for Stream #1

This tier is everything you need to flip the switch on Stream #1 without anything looking broken or unfinished. Specs follow YouTube's current guidelines as of your launch window — double-check before exporting in case YouTube has shifted them.

**Channel-level (one-time setup)**

1. **Channel banner** — 2560×1440 px, PNG or JPG, ≤6 MB. Safe area for text/logo: 1546×423 px centered. Plain background, channel name, tagline, optional schedule line.
2. **Channel avatar / profile picture** — 800×800 px, PNG. Will be displayed as a circle, so keep important content centered and inside a 720 px circle.
3. **Channel watermark** — 150×150 px, transparent PNG. Sits in the corner of every video. Make this a tiny "LL" mark or a clean wordmark.

**OBS full-screen scene cards** (1920×1080 px PNG, transparent or solid, your choice)

4. `Starting Soon` card
5. `BRB` card
6. `Stream Ended / Thanks` card

You can make all three from one template — same layout, different headline. Keep type large enough to read on a phone. Leave a quiet zone at the bottom for chat overlay if you embed one.

**On-camera framing**

7. **Webcam frame / cam border** — transparent PNG sized to your cam placement (often 480×360 or 640×360 px). Optional but instantly looks more "produced." A simple 4–8 px border is enough.
8. **Lower-third name tag** — transparent PNG, ~600×100 px. `Loudon · Loudon Live`.

**Audio**

9. **One royalty-free background music loop** for the Starting Soon / BRB cards. 30–60 seconds, loopable, low-key. Sources: Epidemic Sound, Artlist, FreeMusicArchive, or your own. Do NOT use copyrighted music — even quietly. YouTube will catch it.
10. **Mic check sweep / line check tone** — optional, but useful. A 5-second 1 kHz tone or pink-noise burst you can play before going live to confirm levels.

**One-time content**

11. **Channel trailer video** — 45–75 sec. Use the script in §3. This sits at the top of your channel for non-subscribers. You can record this on Stream #1's setup day.

That's the MVP list. With those eleven items, you can go live tonight without anything looking embarrassing.

---

## 8. Media & asset list — Nice-to-have (first month)

Add these as you have time. None of them are blockers.

**Visual polish**

- Animated `Starting Soon` countdown (5-min countdown is the standard).
- Stream stinger / transition (1–2 sec) between scenes.
- Short channel intro animation (3–5 sec) at the start of VODs.
- A second scene background (e.g., a "talking head" scene vs. a "build" scene that shows your editor full-screen).
- Topic title card per stream — same template, swap the topic line. Builds visual consistency across VODs.
- Outro card with subscribe prompt + "next stream: [date]" line.
- Thumbnail template for VODs — 1280×720 px. Three or four variants you can swap a topic word into.

**Functional overlays**

- Chat overlay on stream (so chat is visible to VOD viewers later).
- Q&A / "chat question" callout overlay.
- "Code on screen" / "patch on screen" lower-third you can toggle when you switch to a screen-share scene.
- Stream alerts (new sub, new follow) if you want them — keep them quiet and short.

**Audio**

- A small library of 3–5 background loops you rotate so standby music doesn't get repetitive.
- A few short sound effects (scene change, alert, "let's go") — use sparingly.

**Channel maintenance**

- Pinned community post: a short "what this channel is" intro for first-time visitors.
- VOD chapter style guide for yourself, so chapters look consistent across streams.
- Playlist structure (e.g., "Sound from first principles," "Synth lab," "Music technique," "Live builds") — start adding VODs to playlists from stream #1 forward.
- A simple custom end screen layout you reuse on every VOD.

**Brand-y stuff (only if you want)**

- A wordmark / logo refinement past the MVP avatar.
- Custom emoji set (only matters once you turn on memberships).
- A short site or landing page that links the channel + any other Loudon Live work.

## 9. Pre-flight checklist for Stream #1

The minimum sequence to actually go live, in order:

1. Channel banner, avatar, watermark uploaded.
2. About / description filled in.
3. Three OBS scenes built: `Starting Soon`, `Live`, `BRB`. (Stream-end card optional but easy.)
4. Audio levels checked — mic, system audio, music loop.
5. One royalty-free music loop assigned to `Starting Soon` and `BRB`.
6. Stream key plugged into OBS, test stream done as Unlisted at least once.
7. Stream title and description drafted using the §4 template.
8. Going-live post drafted in advance (don't write it while live).
9. Phone or second device open to YouTube to confirm what viewers actually see.
10. Go.

Channel trailer can be recorded and uploaded after Stream #1 — it's higher-leverage once there's a VOD or two for new viewers to follow up with.

I've found the pitch and drafted the rewrite. Two things first: the Concierge didn't come. A hook blocks agent spawns in this session, so I searched on my own and changed nothing in the palace. Midway through, shell access was also turned off, so I didn't open the [[LDN RTM]] page. Its description below comes from the Loudon Live entry.

The pitch lives in `Projects/Loudon Live/Loudon Live — launch kit.md`: the tagline, the About text and the trailer. It's dated May. It came before the 2026-10-14 retune, which made Loud'n Live your teaching and coaching face, says the subject is sound and music rather than tools, and adds Read The Manual (RTM) and coaching. So this rewrite brings it up to date as well as trying to pull more viewers.

---

**Tagline**

> Synths and effects built from scratch, and why they sound the way they do.

**About**

> I build synths and audio effects from scratch, on stream, and dig into why they sound the way they do. For electronic musicians who want to know what's actually happening inside a sound.
>
> Three kinds of video here:
> · Live builds: one project pushed forward per stream, like a synth, a delay or a strange oscillator. The parts that don't work yet stay in.
> · Sound lab: the foundations from first principles. What makes a sound feel warm, why two notes beat against each other, what your ears are doing.
> · Read the Manual: one instrument's whole manual, read and tested, one short video per section.
>
> The tools change with the project: Max, RNBO, Ableton Live, code, hardware, paper. The subject stays sound and music.
>
> I've taught music for a long time, and I coach one-on-one, online and in person: [link]
>
> New videos and streams: [schedule]. Past streams stay up.

**Short bio**

> Synths and effects built from scratch, and why they sound the way they do. Live builds, sound lab, one-on-one coaching.

**Trailer (~50 sec)**

> *[Cold open, no greeting. The Lissajous logo drawing itself; three tones sounding.]*
> This is my logo. You're hearing it too: three tones at the same ratios that draw the shape.
> *[The figure drifts; the chord wobbles.]*
> Hear that slow wobble? That's the shape drifting. The ratios are almost whole numbers, but not quite.
> *[Snap to whole numbers. Figure and chord both go still.]*
> Make them whole, and both stop.
> *[Cut to you at the workspace.]*
> I'm Loudon. This is Loud'n Live. That's the whole channel in ten seconds: build something that makes sound, then find out why it sounds that way.
> Some videos are live builds, one project pushed forward, including the parts where it doesn't work yet. Some are sound lab, the foundations from first principles. Some go through one instrument's manual, section by section.
> I've taught music for a long time. Here it's less teaching than working out loud, with you in the room.
> New videos every [day]. Come build something.

---

**What does the work**

- **The first line.** YouTube shows only the opening of the About before "more." The old one opened with a definition ("a creative-technology workshop"). The new one says what you'll see and who it's for.
- **The trailer opens on a sound.** The first few seconds decide whether a new visitor stays.
